title: Even tensor powers of a real sheaf are positive
statement:
Let $\mathcal G_0$ be a lisse
$\iota$-real
Weil sheaf on a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme. Then for every closed point $x$ and every
$k\ge1$, with $\mathcal G_0^{\otimes k}$ the $k$-fold tensor power of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations]:

1. **(i)** the local characteristic polynomial
$\iota\det(1-tF_x,\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x})$ has real
coefficients;
1. **(ii)** if $k$ is even, the power series
$$
\iota\det(1-tF_x,\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x})^{-1}
=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nt^n
$$
has all coefficients $a_n\ge0$, and its constant term is $1$.

proof.text: Fix x and write A for the local Frobenius of G. For every j and k >= 1, prove Tr(Frob(G tensor-power k)^j) = Tr(A^j)^k by induction on k. The base is k=1. The Frobenius-equivariant stalkTensorObjEquiv identifies the successor stalk with the tensor product of the two stalks [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. TensorProduct.map_pow and Mathlib LinearMap.trace_tensorProduct' give the induction step directly, without calculating tensor spectra.

By [def-wf-iota-real] the local polynomial of G is real. Use FrobeniusModule.isReal_iff_forall_trace_pow (Newton identities, obtained from the differentiated trace-determinant identity [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant]) to deduce that every embedded Tr(A^j) is fixed by conjugation. Its kth power is therefore fixed as well. The same criterion and step 1 prove reality of the kth tensor stalk. For even k this power is an even power of a real number, hence nonnegative.

Let s be the multiset of embedded characteristic roots of the tensor-stalk Frobenius. Existing LinearMap.trace_pow_eq_sum_pow_roots_charpoly identifies its jth power sum with the embedded trace, hence with the even power from steps 1 and 2. Existing LinearMap.charpolyRev_eq_prod_roots identifies the embedded local polynomial with product (1-cT), c in s; polynomial and power-series coefficient maps preserve this finite product.

source.place: local eigenvalue products and power sums

proof.text: Apply the existing PowerSeries.coeff_inv_prod_one_sub_C_mul_X_nonneg to s and the nonnegative power sums. This API proves the differentiated form of [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant]: if B=product (1-cT), then T(B inverse)'=(B inverse) sum_{j>=1} p_j T^j. Comparing coefficients gives n b_n=sum_{i+j=n,j>0} b_i p_j. Starting with b_0=1, induction proves b_n>=0, since n is a positive real. This is the same formal identity as the source exponential argument. Finally the constant coefficient of a reverse characteristic polynomial is one, coefficient maps preserve it, and the constant coefficient of its inverse is one. All formulas include the zero-dimensional stalk.

source.place: formal trace-determinant identity and final coefficientwise positivity argument

proof_origin.place: source trace-power argument, using existing stalk tensor comparison, Newton reality criterion and differentiated trace-determinant positivity API

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\mathcal G_0$ be a lisse
$\iota$-real
Weil sheaf on a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme. Then for every closed point $x$ and every
$k\ge1$, with $\mathcal G_0^{\otimes k}$ the $k$-fold tensor power of
[def-real-weil-representation-operations]:

**(i)** the local characteristic polynomial
$\iota\det(1-tF_x,\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x})$ has real
coefficients;
**(ii)** if $k$ is even, the power series
$$
\iota\det(1-tF_x,\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x})^{-1}
=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nt^n
$$
has all coefficients $a_n\ge0$, and its constant term is $1$.

proof.text:
Let $S_x=\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\}$ be the multiset of
eigenvalues of $F_x$ on $\mathcal G_{0,\bar x}$, counted with
multiplicity. By [def-wf-iota-real] the multiset
$\iota(S_x)$ is stable under complex conjugation. The eigenvalues
of $F_x$ on $\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x}$ are the
$k$-fold products $\alpha_{i_1}\cdots\alpha_{i_k}$ ([p-linear-spectra]), and the
multiset of their $\iota$-images is again conjugation-stable, which
proves (i). For (ii), with $k=2k'$ even, the elementary formal
identity

$$
\det(1-tM)^{-1}=\exp\Bigl(\sum_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Tr}(M^n)\frac{t^n}{n}\Bigr)
$$

(valid for every endomorphism $M$ of finite rank; a power-series
identity, per the README allowance for elementary infinite-series
calculus) gives, for the operator $M=F_x$ on
$\mathcal G^{\otimes k}_{0,\bar x}$,

$$
\operatorname{Tr}(M^n)
=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl((F_x^n)^{\otimes k}\bigr)
=\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^n)^{k},
$$

because the eigenvalues of $M^n$ are the $k$-fold products
$\alpha_{i_1}^n\cdots\alpha_{i_k}^n$ and
$\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_k}\alpha_{i_1}^n\cdots\alpha_{i_k}^n= \bigl(\sum_i\alpha_i^n\bigr)^k$. Since the conjugate of
$\iota(S_x)$ is $\iota(S_x)$ itself, the number
$\iota(\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^n))$ is real, so

$$
\iota(\operatorname{Tr}(M^n))
=\iota(\operatorname{Tr}(F_x^n))^{2k'}\ge0,
$$

and every coefficient of the exponential series is a finite sum of
products of nonnegative reals, hence nonnegative; the constant term
is $1$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-7a767d503 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and every cited statement; review.md has the details. The statement is word for word the main-20261015 blueprint statement and is not weakened. The only statement-dependency change adds def-wf-iota-real, which the hypothesis uses. Step 1: the tensor action from def-real-weil-representation-operations, the conjugation-stable eigenvalues from def-wf-iota-real and the tensor-product eigenvalues from p-linear-spectra, applied k times, give B(t). A permutation σ with conj z_i = z_{σ(i)} permutes the factors of B(t), so its coefficients are real, which proves (i). Step 2: applying ι entrywise to the matrix commutes with determinants and with the tensor-product matrix. p-linear-triangular is applied over C, which is algebraically closed; its proof, unit and Lean (IsAlgClosed) all carry that hypothesis. This gives Tr(M^n)=s_n^k, with s_n real, so the trace is ≥0 when k is even. Reading the diagonal off det(1-tM) misses zero eigenvalues, but this is harmless: F_x is invertible, and zero entries add nothing to the traces. Step 3: lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant needs a characteristic-zero field, finite dimension and an endomorphism; C and M_C satisfy all three, and the inverse is unique because B(0)=1. Step 4 is elementary: it is the coefficient formula of def-weil-power-series-exponential with R=C. Edge cases tested: V=0, the empty scheme, k=1 (eigenvalue -1 shows parity is needed), a conjugate pair ±i, and a Jordan block. There are no new nodes, no duplicate (searched for 'nonnegative coefficients' and 'even tensor') and no cycle. Accepted tool use: lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant (sec-zeta-weil), a generic identity that is exactly the one the unit's step 1 uses; it cites no trace-formula or Poincaré-duality node. Batch-5 flag on p-linear-triangular (sec-trace-formula): it is genuinely outside both assumptions. It is generic Schur triangularization with no dependencies and closed, sorry-free Lean. It is already in the item's closure through p-linear-spectra, and this unit lists it in its uses and its step 1. It is not a step of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proof, so no assumption leaf is needed. Separate observation, not a fault here: the imported statement text of p-linear-triangular omits 'algebraically closed' and should be aligned later. No changes made.

lean.statement: theorem isReal_tensorPower_and_even_nonneg {l : ℕ} [Fact l.Prime] {k₀ : Type u} [Field k₀] [Finite k₀] [Fact (ringChar k₀ ≠ l)] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀))] (ι : PadicAlgCl l ≃+* ℂ) (G : WeilSheaf k₀ l X) (hG : G.IsLisse) (hreal : G.IsReal ι.toRingHom) (x : X.finitePoints) (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : ((Nat.iterate (fun H => G.tensorObj H hG) (k - 1) G).stalk x).IsReal ι.toRingHom ∧ (Even k → (∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤ PowerSeries.coeff n (((Polynomial.map ι.toRingHom ((Nat.iterate (fun H => G.tensorObj H hG) (k - 1) G).stalk x).localPolynomial : Polynomial ℂ) : PowerSeries ℂ)⁻¹)) ∧ PowerSeries.constantCoeff (((Polynomial.map ι.toRingHom ((Nat.iterate (fun H => G.tensorObj H hG) (k - 1) G).stalk x).localPolynomial : Polynomial ℂ) : PowerSeries ℂ)⁻¹) = 1)
